shortlist.author: self
shortlist.quote:
Let’s go back to childhood. This will be a vulnerable one…

I’ve learned that certificates aren’t what makes someone great at what they’re qualified for; rather, it’s the experiences and energy a person carries, as part of them is in that practice, which is why they do what they do.

Younger me already knew that she wanted to help people, as she saw how much pain there is in the world, even around her, as she carried the pain of those who shouldn’t have laid it on her. But with that pain, there’s also love, but love with patience, kindness, understanding, and choice.

Not knowing much but the thought of helping others, I eventually studied psychology. My journey in spirituality began with the first year I started my journey to obtain my degree. I started to feel that psychology was kind of soulless, and the question was planted, that lead me to a chapter that started it all…

#innerchildwork #innerchildhealing #innerwork #healingjourney #childhoodhealing

shortlist.author: self
shortlist.quote:
18-year-old me used to wake up at 5am so she had time to do yoga before school.
She would sit down in silence with the sunrise to a YouTube guided meditation. And to her, she found peace in that, even when she knew no one around her was doing similar practices. 

During the pandemic, tarot found her. She got a deck and went straight to intuitively reading the cards for her friends. “How was that so accurate?” “That’s definitely what I’m going through.” And she would secretly pull a card for herself and journal her reflections. Somehow, she found herself waking up at 5am again to do yoga, meditate to Dr Joe Dispenza, and gradually opened herself up to meeting her guides, even though she used to chant for her third eye to close in hopes of not seeing those things lurking in shadows. And from then on, she started to see the light with the gift and no longer the fear.

Diving more into introspection, countless afternoon meditations with an amethyst balancing on her forehead, and a few months in, she sat beside her cousin and childhood friend and burst out a suggestion: let’s go up to the rooftop and meditate. Just follow my voice.
They shared their visions and what they felt, and for her, it felt natural and she was also amazed of the simple presence shared in silence and deep breaths.

Then I moved abroad. More of this journey later… 

Photos from 2018-2021

#spiritualpath #spiritualawakening #spirituality

shortlist.author: self
shortlist.quote:
Forgotten to meal prep? You’re human. 😂

This is exactly why I encourage my clients to have a Plan B.

Not every week goes to plan. Life gets busy, meetings run over, the food shop gets pushed back…

The women who stay consistent aren’t the ones who meal prep perfectly every Sunday.

They’re the ones who know what to do when they don’t.

Save this for the next time you open the fridge and think, “I’ve got nothing to eat.” 💚

shortlist.author: self
shortlist.quote:
The best transformations aren’t just physical. 

Yes, she’s built lean muscle, changed her body composition and created an incredible, strong physique.

But what I’m most proud of is everything you can’t see in the photos.

She’s learnt she can enjoy meals out without feeling guilty.

She’s built consistency instead of chasing perfection.

And she’s started trusting herself again.

One thing she said that really stuck with me was:

“With life in general I’m not procrastinating as much. If it has to be done, just do it now and it’s done.”

That right there is what coaching is about.

Because when you start keeping the promises you make to yourself in the gym, it often spills over into the rest of your life too.

The physical results are amazing… but the person you’re becoming along the way is the real transformation. 💚

If you’re ready to build a stronger body and an even stronger mindset, my DMs are always open.

shortlist.author: self
shortlist.quote:
“I can’t be bothered to cook” doesn’t have to automatically mean takeaway 😂

Some of my most consistent meals are also the ones that require the least effort.

Think freezer staples, microwave rice, wraps, eggs, cooked chicken and anything I can throw in the air fryer.

You don’t need to cook everything from scratch to eat well.

Sometimes the best meal is simply the one you’ll actually make. 

Save this for the next time you’re standing in front of the fridge thinking “I cannot be bothered" 🤷🏻‍♀️

shortlist.author: self
shortlist.quote:
If you’re not losing weight despite going to the gym regularly, here’s why…

You can’t out-train a poor diet 🍩🍟🍕

Regardless of how often you go to the gym or how hard you train…

If you’re not maintaining a caloric deficit with adequate protein, you won’t see much in terms of fat loss.

Try this:

1. Take your goal weight and multiply it by 11. Start there for your daily calories.

2. Take your goal weight and multiply it by 0.83. Start there for your daily protein.

Commit to tracking your food intake honestly and accurately for 6 months hitting the above targets, and I guarantee you’ll see significant fat-loss results.

And to make sure you don’t get “skinny fat”…

Make sure you’re hitting the weights hard 3-4 days per week as well.

Finish this off with a 7x7 step goal (7k steps, 7 days per week) and you now have the formula for an enjoyable and sustainable fat-loss transformation.

Good luck and remember, I’m always here if you need help.

shortlist.author: self
shortlist.quote:
9 rules for operating like an ambitious healthy Dubai CEO.

(From 10 years of coaching executives, founders, and entrepreneurs)

There are hundreds of health "guides" out there for busy professionals.

But not enough simple, actionable systems built for how executives actually live.

So here's the one I use with every client:

1. Treat your body like a business
↳ Get baseline data. Bloods, body comp, resting heart rate.
↳ If it doesn't get measured, it doesn't get managed.

2. Train at least 3x a week
↳ Three structured sessions beat six random ones. Every time.
↳ Leave reps in the tank. Consistency beats intensity.

3. Protect sleep like you protect your calendar
↳ 7+ hours. Non-negotiable.
↳ People who function on under six hours? Rounded up, that's zero.

4. Eat enough protein across 4 meals
↳ Your body can only absorb so much per sitting.
↳ A shake at 3pm and steak at 9 isn't a plan.

5. Build a decision framework for food
↳ Hotels, client dinners, airports. You need rules that travel.
↳ Rigid meal plans break. Frameworks survive anything.

6. Review your data weekly
↳ Weekly averages over daily weigh-ins. Always.
↳ One bad Tuesday is noise. An 8-week trend is signal.

7. Build recovery as a system
↳ Recovery and training volume need to match.
↳ One outgrows the other, you get under-recovered.

8. Set a 90-day body composition target
↳ Write it down. "From X kg to Y kg by this date."
↳ Vague goals get vague results. Be specific.

9. Build autonomy, not dependency
↳ The goal is results you can keep without a coach.
↳ If the system only works when someone runs it, it's not yours.

You don't need another app.
You don't need another supplement stack.

You need a system that ties the basics together and runs on data, not guesswork.

If you want to see how your current setup stacks up, take the Executive Physique Audit here: https://calendly.com/zofit/1-1-personal-training-video-session

It scores your training, nutrition, and recovery against what we use with clients.

Your health is your choice.

Make the right one

Z

shortlist.author: self
shortlist.quote:
According to Sternberg’s theory, the balance of intimacy, passion, and commitment naturally shifts and evolves over the course of a relationship.

While passion tends to peak quickly before declining and levelling off, and commitment peaks and remains relatively stable, intimacy requires ongoing sharing and emotional connection.

Sternberg emphasizes that relationships are generally at their happiest and most stable when the strength and need of these various three components are similar between both partners.
